pnpm/pnpm (pnpm) ### [`v12.16.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.16.1): pnpm 12.16.1 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.16.0...v12.16.1) This release fixes `pnpm install` hanging on a cold store in workspaces that install Cargo crates, and `pnpm pack` shipping a file that `files` excludes by name. ##### Patch Changes - `pnpm install` no longer hangs on a cold store in a workspace that also installs Cargo crates or a Rust toolchain. - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now apply a `files` entry that names a file after the glob and directory entries, as npm does. A file excluded by name, such as `!dist/index.js`, stays out even when a later `dist/**` matches it. A file named by its path, such as `lib/secret.js`, ships even when a later `!lib/*.js` matches it. - `pnpm install` no longer leaves a broken symlink in an injected workspace dependency when the package links to a file outside its published files and pnpm imports by hardlink. Installing a git dependency now skips internal directory symlinks when importing its files into the store. - `pnpm install` now relinks a command that a workspace project renames into the projects that depend on it when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false` [pnpm/tasks#224](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/224). - `pnpm install` and `pnpm rebuild` now refresh privately hoisted `.bin` shims in `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/.bin` after a dependency build replaces a script target with a native executable [#​17402](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17402). - `pnpm install` now reads a package's manifest to decide its peer dependencies when it updates an existing lockfile, as it does when it resolves from scratch. - Commands, `pnpm --version`, `pnpm self-update`, and invocations with unknown flags now apply the same `packageManager` and `devEngines.packageManager` settings when switching to the pinned pnpm version or recording it in `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `--config.` flags and `lockfileDir` now reach the version switch and lockfile sync on every entry point. Unreadable settings in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or the global `config.yaml` that do not affect the pin decision no longer block the version switch [pnpm/tasks#222](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/222). - pnpm now accepts the `--cache-dir ` flag, as in `pnpm install --cache-dir /tmp/pnpm-cache` [#​17422](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17422). - When the version or range given to `pnpm unpublish` matches every published version, the error now says so and shows the same command with `--force`. Before, the error suggested running `pnpm unpublish @`, the command that had just failed. #### Platinum Sponsors
#### Gold Sponsors
### [`v12.16.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.16.0): pnpm 12.16 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.15.0...v12.16.0) This release adds a global `--env-file` flag, updates to a symlinked `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and `pnpm setup --no-modify-path`. It also fixes two security issues, in zstd decompression and in signing. ##### Minor Changes - Added a repeatable global `--env-file ` flag to load environment variables from dotenv-style files before running a command. Later files override earlier files, variables already in the environment are preserved, and loaded variables are visible to user-level `.npmrc` interpolation and lifecycle scripts [#​7111](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/7111). - pnpm can now update a `pnpm-lock.yaml` that is a symlink. List the directories the lockfile may link into in the `symlinkedLockfileTargetDirs` setting, in the global config or with `PNPM_CONFIG_SYMLINKED_LOCKFILE_TARGET_DIRS`. pnpm writes the update to the file the symlink points to if that file is inside one of these directories. The symlink stays in place. pnpm ignores this setting in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` [#​17222](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17222). - Added a `--no-modify-path` option to `pnpm setup`. It installs pnpm without adding it to `PATH`, leaving the shell config file, the Windows registry, and the GitHub Actions environment files unchanged. `pnpm setup` then prints the lines to add yourself [get.pnpm.io#37](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/get.pnpm.io/issues/37). ##### Patch Changes ##### Security - Fixed memory exposure and allocation handling vulnerabilities when processing zstd-compressed data [#​17388](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/17388). - Signing in pnpm and pnpr no longer uses arithmetic that may leak the private key through timing. This covers shared artifacts, OCI registry tokens, and OIDC login state [advisory](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0387). ##### Installing packages - A dependency symlink that pnpm cannot point at the wanted target now fails the install with an error that names the link. This happens when the filesystem still serves the old link after pnpm removed it, as a `node_modules` served by a virtual filesystem does. pnpm used to remove the link again without end and crashed with a segmentation fault once the thread ran out of stack. - Concurrent workspace installs no longer lose store-index rows when initializing the shared SQLite index [#​17388](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/17388). - Agent skill links now keep the same target across installs when a package version is installed with several sets of peer dependencies. An install no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_AGENT_SKILL_PATH_OCCUPIED` on a skill link that pnpm created for another of those copies [#​17319](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17319). - pnpm now fails at once, without retrying, when a downloaded package archive contains a rejected entry path [#​17205](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17205). - pnpm now builds a git-hosted dependency in every new location it links the dependency into, such as a new global virtual store slot or a fresh `node_modules`. When the side-effects cache holds the build output, pnpm restores it from there. Before, only the install that fetched the dependency built it. This also fixes dependencies that are already in the store [#​17224](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17224). - Changes a `preResolution` hook makes to the lockfiles now take effect. The hook now also runs when pnpm installs from an up-to-date lockfile. An error thrown by the hook now fails the install. - A custom fetcher in the pnpmfile can now call `fetchers.directory` to fetch a package from a local directory. The call rejects with `ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_INTEGRITY` if the lockfile pins an archive integrity for the package. Previously, calling `fetchers.directory` failed with a `TypeError`. - `packageImportMethod: copy` now also applies to packages that have lifecycle scripts or patches. On a filesystem that supports block cloning, such as ReFS or a Dev Drive on Windows, these packages were cloned [#​17195](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17195). - With `nodeLinker: hoisted` and `autoInstallPeers: false`, a package that workspace projects use with different peer versions is now installed once per peer variant, so each project's copy resolves that project's peer [#​17395](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17395). - Under `nodeLinker: hoisted`, `pnpm install` now leaves a patched package that is already in place alone. The same holds for a package whose peers include a patched package, such as every package peering on a patched `react-native` [#​17188](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17188). - With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, an install that stops partway no longer leaves the next install trusting the packages it was replacing. Before, reverting the change that started the stopped install, such as a patch edit, kept the half-replaced package in `node_modules`. ##### Repeat installs and changed settings - A repeat `pnpm install` now acts on a change to these settings. Before, it reported "Already up to date". - `storeDir` or `virtualStoreDir`: it recreates `node_modules`. - `globalVirtualStoreDir`: it links the packages from the new directory. - `virtualStoreDirMaxLength`: it renames the virtual store directories. - `dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds` turned on: it runs the builds it skipped. - `trustLockfile` turned off: it verifies the lockfile. - `pnpm add`, `pnpm remove`, and `pnpm update` now fail if `node_modules` does not match the current settings. Run `pnpm install` to recreate it. Previously, these commands removed and reinstalled `node_modules` without asking. They report: - `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_STORE` if `node_modules` was linked from a different store. - `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_VIRTUAL_STORE` if it was linked from a different virtual store directory. - `ERR_PNPM_MODULES_BREAKING_CHANGE` if it was installed by an incompatible pnpm version, or if `node_modules/.modules.yaml` cannot be read. - `ERR_PNPM_NODE_LINKER_DIFF` if it was installed with a different `nodeLinker`. `pnpm update` now also fails with `ERR_PNPM_HOIST_PATTERN_DIFF` and the other errors `pnpm add` reports for a changed hoist pattern or `virtualStoreDirMaxLength`. - An install filtered to some workspace projects now fails if `node_modules` was installed with a different `nodeLinker`, `hoistPattern`, `publicHoistPattern`, store, or virtual store. Before, it recreated `node_modules` and left the projects it skipped without their dependencies. A `pnpm install` of the whole workspace still recreates `node_modules` [pnpm/tasks#217](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/217). - `pnpm install` and the `verifyDepsBeforeRun` check now notice an edited patch file when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false`. - `pnpm install` now takes its fast path in a workspace with `patchedDependencies` when the previous install ran with another major version of pnpm. - `pnpm install` now relinks the bins of a workspace package when its `bin` field changes, including with `--frozen-lockfile` and an unchanged lockfile. A filtered install relinks them in the selected projects, and the next install that covers the remaining projects relinks them there [#​17324](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17324). - `pnpm install` now removes command shims from `node_modules/.bin` when a workspace dependency renames or removes an entry from its `bin` field [pnpm/tasks#211](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/211). ##### Resolving dependencies and the lockfile - A package that a plain range and a `:` specifier both resolve from one registry is now recorded once in `pnpm-lock.yaml` and installed once. The lockfile key names the registry a package resolved from. When that registry declares a prefix, through `prefix` in `registries` or through `namedRegistries`, the package is keyed `@:` however its dependency was written: with the prefix, as a plain range its scope routes to that registry, or through the default registry. Before, the plain range was keyed `@`, so one tarball was installed twice and `instanceof` checks and module singletons broke between the two copies. The same name and version served by two registries still get separate entries. When several prefixes declare one registry, its packages are keyed by the lexicographically smallest prefix. If a scope you route reaches a registry that also declares a prefix, your next `pnpm install` re-keys those entries, which shows up as a lockfile diff. Commit it. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` installs the lockfile as recorded. - `pnpm install` now resolves a scope's packages again when the scope is routed to another registry in `registries`. Before, the lockfile kept the versions and integrity resolved from the old registry, so the install failed when the new registry did not serve a locked version or served different content. pnpm records in the workspace state which registry each scope routed to, so a fresh clone without that record installs the lockfile as recorded. Changing the default registry resolves nothing again, and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` is unchanged. - When `autoDedupe` is off, a workspace project's dependencies now resolve from its own ranges, like they do with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`. Previously, another project's narrower range could hold them back. For example, `ajv: "*"` now resolves to the latest Ajv even if another project depends on `ajv@^6`. Packages that a project lists in `peerDependencies` still follow the versions other projects use. `pnpm dedupe` and installs with `autoDedupe: true` still pick one version that satisfies every range. Set `autoDedupe: true` if CI runs `pnpm dedupe --check` [#​17235](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17235). - An optional dependency written with a named-registry prefix, such as `work:^1.0.0`, now fails the install when it cannot be resolved but the lockfile already has a matching entry from that registry. Such a dependency was skipped, which removed its entries from the lockfile. - With `injectWorkspacePackages: true`, a `workspace:` dependency written as a relative path, such as `workspace:../lib-a`, in a workspace package now resolves from that package's directory [#​17284](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17284). - Fixed `pnpm install` failing with `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL` when a workspace package injected through a relative path, such as `workspace:../lib`, has `catalog:` dependencies. Their catalog entries now resolve the way they do for a package injected by name [#​17280](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17280). - `pnpm dedupe` now refreshes cached registry metadata while re-resolving locked versions [#​17208](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17208). - `pnpm dedupe --check` no longer fails when the only difference is a `deprecated` notice that the registry added or removed after the lockfile was written [#​17198](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17198). - Installs delegated to a pnpr server now resolve every prefix declared for a registry URL. A dependency or lockfile entry that used the second of two prefixes for the same registry, such as `zeta:` next to `work:` in `namedRegistries`, failed on the server [pnpm/tasks#204](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/204). - Registry revisions are now addressed at `/@+r` [pnpm/tasks#208](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/208). ##### Adding packages and global packages - `pnpm add @` and `pnpm add @` now install the version the tag or range resolves to, even when the saved range allows a newer one [#​17234](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17234). - `pnpm add ` without a version now installs the version under the dist-tag set by the `tag` setting. An `npm:` alias or a `jsr:` dependency without a version resolves that tag too. The setting is read from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, the global config, `PNPM_CONFIG_TAG`, and `--config.tag`, and defaults to `latest`. - `pnpm add` now accepts the lowercase short options `-p`, `-d`, `-o`, and `-e` as aliases of `--save-prod`, `--save-dev`, `--save-optional`, and `--save-exact`. - `pnpm -D install ` now saves the package to devDependencies. An `add` option such as `-D` or `-E` written before `install ` was rejected as an unexpected argument. - `pnpm add -T` now reports that the short option is ambiguous and points to `--save-types` and `--tilde`. - Global packages installed with `pnpm add -g` are now linked from the global virtual store, so global packages that share dependencies share one copy. Set `virtualStoreType: project` to give each global install its own virtual store. - `pnpm add -g` and the other `--global` commands now fail with `ERR_PNPM_CONFIG_CONFLICT_VIRTUAL_STORE_DIR_WITH_GLOBAL` when `--virtual-store-dir` is passed. A custom `--hoist-pattern` fails with `ERR_PNPM_CONFIG_CONFLICT_HOIST_PATTERN_WITH_GLOBAL`. Passing `--link-workspace-packages`, `--shared-workspace-lockfile`, or `--config.lockfile-dir` with `--global` also fails, with the matching `ERR_PNPM_CONFIG_CONFLICT_*_WITH_GLOBAL` code. ##### Registries, proxies, and login - pnpm now reads the `strictSsl` and `localAddress` settings from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, the global `config.yaml`, `PNPM_CONFIG_*` environment variables, and `--config.*` options. This includes `pnpm self-update` and the download of the pnpm version pinned in `packageManager`. Before, pnpm read them only from `.npmrc` as `strict-ssl` and `local-address` and ignored the other sources [pnpm/tasks#201](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/201). - When Corepack runs pnpm and the native binary has to be downloaded, the download now uses the proxy from pnpm's config. That proxy comes from `PNPM_CONFIG_HTTPS_PROXY` and the matching variables, the global `config.yaml`, and the user `.npmrc`. Previously, the download read the proxy only from `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, and `NO_PROXY` [pnpm/tasks#215](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/215). - When the `pnpm` package downloads its native binary on first run, as it does under Corepack, it now trusts the CA certificates from the `ca`, `ca[]`, and `cafile` settings of `.npmrc`, including the ones scoped to the registry. A registry behind a private CA failed with `fetch failed` before, unless `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` named the CA. A project `.npmrc` is used only while the download is checked against npm's signature. Node.js versions that cannot add CA certificates after startup still need `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`. - `pnpm login` saves the token in `/auth.ini` again. Since v12.1.0, an unscoped login had made its registry the default for every project that did not name a registry. A login now also removes the token an earlier login saved for that registry or scope under `_auth` in the global `config.yaml`. `pnpm login --scope` still routes the scope through the global `registries` setting. - pnpm no longer warns that a `registries` entry routed through the `@` scope matches no configured registry. pnpm applied such an entry and its options such as `serverType` while reporting it as ignored [pnpm/tasks#184](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/184). ##### Running scripts and other commands - `pnpm ci --lockfile` and `pnpm ci --config.lockfile=true` no longer delete `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `pnpm ci` now always keeps the lockfile and runs a frozen install from it. - `pnpm deploy --legacy` now checks the workspace lockfile against `minimumReleaseAge` and the other resolution policies, as `pnpm install` does, and fails with `ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION` when a locked version is too new. It used to deploy an older version that is not in the lockfile without a warning [#​17209](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17209). - `pnpm deploy` now keeps a deployed symlink to a directory inside the project even if the directory is not among the deployed files, such as a link into `node_modules` [#​17288](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17288). - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now keep `pnpm.config` in the published `package.json`. They also always include the file `pnpm.config` points to in the tarball [#​17210](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17210). - `pnpm -r publish --batch` now sends `PUT /-/pnpr/v0/publish`, the batch publish endpoint that pnpr serves. - `pnpm audit --ignore` and `pnpm audit --ignore-unfixable` now exit with a non-zero code when vulnerabilities at or above the audit level remain after ignoring. Before, these commands always exited with code 0. - `pnpm audit --fix` and `pnpm audit --interactive` now fail with `ERR_PNPM_AUDIT_FIX_WITH_IGNORE` when combined with `--ignore` or `--ignore-unfixable`. Before, the fix ran and the ignore flags had no effect. - `pnpm -r run

##### Minor Changes

- [#​3057](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3057) [`c05225a`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/c05225a636c679870b65f8ca4fe83a76ea1cf113) Thanks [@​steipete](https://redirect.github.com/steipete)! - `ServerEvent` takes optional `params`, which the `subscriptions/listen` router delivers with its own subscription ID, so a gateway can forward change notifications with their `_meta` and extension params.

- [#​3047](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3047) [`46d9c99`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/46d9c9921b6542e813c1ecc5f9fc964085e8e3bb) Thanks [@​KKonstantinov](https://redirect.github.com/KKonstantinov), [@​tobi-oye](https://redirect.github.com/tobi-oye), [@​mattzcarey](https://redirect.github.com/mattzcarey)! - Add the Skills extension (SEP-2640), reachable through new `ext/skills` subpaths; package root exports are unchanged.

  - `@modelcontextprotocol/server/ext/skills`: `SkillsExtension` (`attach(server)` serves `skills/list`, `skills/get`, `resources/directory/read` and a `skill://{+path}` resource template), `SkillsExtension.load(files)` returning a `SkillCatalog` with `entries` and `reload()`, the `SkillFiles` storage adapter with `memorySkillFiles`, `SkillSource` for generated catalogs, `skillEntry`, and `SkillCatalogError`. Invalid skills are skipped with a warning (`onWarning`), or fail under `strict`. A file whose bytes are valid UTF-8 is served as `text`, whatever its MIME type; any other file as a base64 `blob`.
  - `@modelcontextprotocol/server/ext/skills/node`: `loadSkills(folder)` and `nodeSkillFiles(folder)`.
  - `@modelcontextprotocol/client/ext/skills`: `SkillsClient` with `list()` (throws on an invalid entry; `skipInvalid: true` keeps the valid ones and returns the rest in `invalid`), `get()`, `read(skill, path?)` (size, digest and `SKILL.md` frontmatter verified, `SkillVerificationError` on a mismatch; a copy from the response cache that fails a check is fetched once more with `cacheMode: 'refresh'` first) and `readDirectory()`.
  - `@modelcontextprotocol/core/ext/skills`: schemas, types and constants, including `SKILL_LIMITS`. The result schemas follow the stable spec, so `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` are required.

  `SkillsExtension.attach` is `@experimental`: how an extension is wired to a server may change in a minor release. The rest of the Skills API is stable.

  Works on 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28. On 2026-07-28 only, the server sends the caching fields (`ttlMs`, `cacheScope`), and `SkillsClient` requires them and returns them from `list()`, `get()` and `readDirectory()`.

##### Patch Changes

- [#​3083](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3083) [`ef38c67`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/ef38c6765a15ee29030340dfea28b013893fa0a2) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - The bundled Ajv validator is now built with fast-uri 3.1.8 (was 3.1.0). fast-uri 3.1.6 and later reject a `$id` or `$ref` whose text before the first colon is not a valid URI scheme (`my_tool:output`), or whose URN namespace is not valid (`urn:my_tool:output`): a schema that uses one no longer compiles, and a tool that carries it fails with an invalid-schema error. An underscore without a colon (`my_tool_output`) and a `$ref` into `#/$defs/...` or `#/definitions/...` are not affected.

- [#​2960](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2960) [`43c45f4`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/43c45f4941d824e7251a7d1266823a84af90fab3) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - A server whose tool puts `x-mcp-header` on a `number`-typed parameter keeps checking that tool's `Mcp-Param-*` headers on `tools/call`, as 2.3.0 does: a header that is missing for a value in the body, or that disagrees with the body, is answered `400` with JSON-RPC error `-32020`. Clients on a 2026-07-28 connection other than stdio no longer list such a tool and send no `Mcp-Param-*` headers for it, so a call that carries a value for a declared parameter is rejected the same way; the server logs a warning each time tools are listed. Use an integer (`z.int()`) or remove the annotation.

- [#​3081](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3081) [`5820f79`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/5820f796a48ae6b8e756a7fbfd627e7e2e1ac891) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - A tool `outputSchema` whose root is a `$ref` to a `type: "object"` entry of its own `$defs` or `definitions` (what zod writes for `z.object({...}).meta({ id })`), or a union of such refs, is now treated as an object schema. On 2025-era connections the tool's schema and `structuredContent` are no longer wrapped in `{ result: ... }`, so a 2025-era client that read `structuredContent.result` for such a tool now reads `structuredContent`. On every era the advertised schema gains `type: "object"` at its root.

- [#​3057](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3057) [`c05225a`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/c05225a636c679870b65f8ca4fe83a76ea1cf113) Thanks [@​steipete](https://redirect.github.com/steipete)! - Connecting a `Server` or `McpServer` to a `PerRequestHTTPServerTransport` classified at a modern revision that `supportedProtocolVersions` lists and the SDK implements now binds that revision, instead of answering `-32022`.

- [#​3005](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3005) [`b381559`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/b381559edc0dbe25ab8324cada345b49bd1d2fc4) Thanks [@​chaeyn](https://redirect.github.com/chaeyn)! - Reflect resource and resource template `update({ title })` changes in list responses. - [#​3002](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3002) [`895007f`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/895007fe728b9c57fbe3ed45fe279ddc51f731f7) Thanks [@​Hugo-DDT](https://redirect.github.com/Hugo-DDT)! - `createMcpHandler` now sends `Allow: POST` on every `405` it answers to a non-POST request, with `legacy: 'stateless'` (the default) and with `legacy: 'reject'`.

### [`v12.16.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.16.1): pnpm 12.16.1

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.16.0...v12.16.1)

This release fixes `pnpm install` hanging on a cold store in workspaces that install Cargo crates, and `pnpm pack` shipping a file that `files` excludes by name.

##### Patch Changes

- `pnpm install` no longer hangs on a cold store in a workspace that also installs Cargo crates or a Rust toolchain.

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now apply a `files` entry that names a file after the glob and directory entries, as npm does. A file excluded by name, such as `!dist/index.js`, stays out even when a later `dist/**` matches it. A file named by its path, such as `lib/secret.js`, ships even when a later `!lib/*.js` matches it.

- `pnpm install` no longer leaves a broken symlink in an injected workspace dependency when the package links to a file outside its published files and pnpm imports by hardlink. Installing a git dependency now skips internal directory symlinks when importing its files into the store.

- `pnpm install` now relinks a command that a workspace project renames into the projects that depend on it when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false` [pnpm/tasks#224](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/224).

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm rebuild` now refresh privately hoisted `.bin` shims in `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/.bin` after a dependency build replaces a script target with a native executable [#​17402](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17402).

- `pnpm install` now reads a package's manifest to decide its peer dependencies when it updates an existing lockfile, as it does when it resolves from scratch.

- Commands, `pnpm --version`, `pnpm self-update`, and invocations with unknown flags now apply the same `packageManager` and `devEngines.packageManager` settings when switching to the pinned pnpm version or recording it in `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `--config.<key>` flags and `lockfileDir` now reach the version switch and lockfile sync on every entry point. Unreadable settings in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or the global `config.yaml` that do not affect the pin decision no longer block the version switch [pnpm/tasks#222](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/222).

- pnpm now accepts the `--cache-dir <dir>` flag, as in `pnpm install --cache-dir /tmp/pnpm-cache` [#​17422](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17422).

- When the version or range given to `pnpm unpublish` matches every published version, the error now says so and shows the same command with `--force`. Before, the error suggested running `pnpm unpublish <pkg>@<version>`, the command that had just failed.

### [`v12.16.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.16.0): pnpm 12.16

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.15.0...v12.16.0)

This release adds a global `--env-file` flag, updates to a symlinked `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and `pnpm setup --no-modify-path`. It also fixes two security issues, in zstd decompression and in signing.

##### Minor Changes

- Added a repeatable global `--env-file <path>` flag to load environment variables from dotenv-style files before running a command. Later files override earlier files, variables already in the environment are preserved, and loaded variables are visible to user-level `.npmrc` interpolation and lifecycle scripts [#​7111](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/7111).

- pnpm can now update a `pnpm-lock.yaml` that is a symlink. List the directories the lockfile may link into in the `symlinkedLockfileTargetDirs` setting, in the global config or with `PNPM_CONFIG_SYMLINKED_LOCKFILE_TARGET_DIRS`. pnpm writes the update to the file the symlink points to if that file is inside one of these directories. The symlink stays in place. pnpm ignores this setting in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` [#​17222](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17222).

- Added a `--no-modify-path` option to `pnpm setup`. It installs pnpm without adding it to `PATH`, leaving the shell config file, the Windows registry, and the GitHub Actions environment files unchanged. `pnpm setup` then prints the lines to add yourself [get.pnpm.io#37](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/get.pnpm.io/issues/37).

##### Patch Changes

##### Security

- Fixed memory exposure and allocation handling vulnerabilities when processing zstd-compressed data [#​17388](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/17388).

- Signing in pnpm and pnpr no longer uses arithmetic that may leak the private key through timing. This covers shared artifacts, OCI registry tokens, and OIDC login state [advisory](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0387).

##### Installing packages

- A dependency symlink that pnpm cannot point at the wanted target now fails the install with an error that names the link. This happens when the filesystem still serves the old link after pnpm removed it, as a `node_modules` served by a virtual filesystem does. pnpm used to remove the link again without end and crashed with a segmentation fault once the thread ran out of stack.

- Concurrent workspace installs no longer lose store-index rows when initializing the shared SQLite index [#​17388](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/17388).

- Agent skill links now keep the same target across installs when a package version is installed with several sets of peer dependencies. An install no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_AGENT_SKILL_PATH_OCCUPIED` on a skill link that pnpm created for another of those copies [#​17319](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17319).

- pnpm now fails at once, without retrying, when a downloaded package archive contains a rejected entry path [#​17205](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17205).

- pnpm now builds a git-hosted dependency in every new location it links the dependency into, such as a new global virtual store slot or a fresh `node_modules`. When the side-effects cache holds the build output, pnpm restores it from there. Before, only the install that fetched the dependency built it. This also fixes dependencies that are already in the store [#​17224](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17224).

- Changes a `preResolution` hook makes to the lockfiles now take effect. The hook now also runs when pnpm installs from an up-to-date lockfile. An error thrown by the hook now fails the install.

- A custom fetcher in the pnpmfile can now call `fetchers.directory` to fetch a package from a local directory. The call rejects with `ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_INTEGRITY` if the lockfile pins an archive integrity for the package. Previously, calling `fetchers.directory` failed with a `TypeError`.

- `packageImportMethod: copy` now also applies to packages that have lifecycle scripts or patches. On a filesystem that supports block cloning, such as ReFS or a Dev Drive on Windows, these packages were cloned [#​17195](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17195).

- With `nodeLinker: hoisted` and `autoInstallPeers: false`, a package that workspace projects use with different peer versions is now installed once per peer variant, so each project's copy resolves that project's peer [#​17395](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17395).

- Under `nodeLinker: hoisted`, `pnpm install` now leaves a patched package that is already in place alone. The same holds for a package whose peers include a patched package, such as every package peering on a patched `react-native` [#​17188](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17188).

- With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, an install that stops partway no longer leaves the next install trusting the packages it was replacing. Before, reverting the change that started the stopped install, such as a patch edit, kept the half-replaced package in `node_modules`.

##### Repeat installs and changed settings

- A repeat `pnpm install` now acts on a change to these settings. Before, it reported "Already up to date".

  - `storeDir` or `virtualStoreDir`: it recreates `node_modules`.
  - `globalVirtualStoreDir`: it links the packages from the new directory.
  - `virtualStoreDirMaxLength`: it renames the virtual store directories.
  - `dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds` turned on: it runs the builds it skipped.
  - `trustLockfile` turned off: it verifies the lockfile.

- `pnpm add`, `pnpm remove`, and `pnpm update` now fail if `node_modules` does not match the current settings. Run `pnpm install` to recreate it. Previously, these commands removed and reinstalled `node_modules` without asking. They report:

  - `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_STORE` if `node_modules` was linked from a different store.
  - `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_VIRTUAL_STORE` if it was linked from a different virtual store directory.
  - `ERR_PNPM_MODULES_BREAKING_CHANGE` if it was installed by an incompatible pnpm version, or if `node_modules/.modules.yaml` cannot be read.
  - `ERR_PNPM_NODE_LINKER_DIFF` if it was installed with a different `nodeLinker`.

  `pnpm update` now also fails with `ERR_PNPM_HOIST_PATTERN_DIFF` and the other errors `pnpm add` reports for a changed hoist pattern or `virtualStoreDirMaxLength`.

- An install filtered to some workspace projects now fails if `node_modules` was installed with a different `nodeLinker`, `hoistPattern`, `publicHoistPattern`, store, or virtual store. Before, it recreated `node_modules` and left the projects it skipped without their dependencies. A `pnpm install` of the whole workspace still recreates `node_modules` [pnpm/tasks#217](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/217).

- `pnpm install` and the `verifyDepsBeforeRun` check now notice an edited patch file when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false`.

- `pnpm install` now takes its fast path in a workspace with `patchedDependencies` when the previous install ran with another major version of pnpm.

- `pnpm install` now relinks the bins of a workspace package when its `bin` field changes, including with `--frozen-lockfile` and an unchanged lockfile. A filtered install relinks them in the selected projects, and the next install that covers the remaining projects relinks them there [#​17324](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17324).

- `pnpm install` now removes command shims from `node_modules/.bin` when a workspace dependency renames or removes an entry from its `bin` field [pnpm/tasks#211](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/211).

##### Resolving dependencies and the lockfile

- A package that a plain range and a `<prefix>:` specifier both resolve from one registry is now recorded once in `pnpm-lock.yaml` and installed once. The lockfile key names the registry a package resolved from. When that registry declares a prefix, through `prefix` in `registries` or through `namedRegistries`, the package is keyed `<name>@<prefix>:<version>` however its dependency was written: with the prefix, as a plain range its scope routes to that registry, or through the default registry. Before, the plain range was keyed `<name>@<version>`, so one tarball was installed twice and `instanceof` checks and module singletons broke between the two copies. The same name and version served by two registries still get separate entries. When several prefixes declare one registry, its packages are keyed by the lexicographically smallest prefix.

  If a scope you route reaches a registry that also declares a prefix, your next `pnpm install` re-keys those entries, which shows up as a lockfile diff. Commit it. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` installs the lockfile as recorded.

- `pnpm install` now resolves a scope's packages again when the scope is routed to another registry in `registries`. Before, the lockfile kept the versions and integrity resolved from the old registry, so the install failed when the new registry did not serve a locked version or served different content. pnpm records in the workspace state which registry each scope routed to, so a fresh clone without that record installs the lockfile as recorded. Changing the default registry resolves nothing again, and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` is unchanged.

- When `autoDedupe` is off, a workspace project's dependencies now resolve from its own ranges, like they do with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`. Previously, another project's narrower range could hold them back. For example, `ajv: "*"` now resolves to the latest Ajv even if another project depends on `ajv@^6`. Packages that a project lists in `peerDependencies` still follow the versions other projects use. `pnpm dedupe` and installs with `autoDedupe: true` still pick one version that satisfies every range. Set `autoDedupe: true` if CI runs `pnpm dedupe --check` [#​17235](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17235).

- An optional dependency written with a named-registry prefix, such as `work:^1.0.0`, now fails the install when it cannot be resolved but the lockfile already has a matching entry from that registry. Such a dependency was skipped, which removed its entries from the lockfile.

- With `injectWorkspacePackages: true`, a `workspace:` dependency written as a relative path, such as `workspace:../lib-a`, in a workspace package now resolves from that package's directory [#​17284](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17284).

- Fixed `pnpm install` failing with `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL` when a workspace package injected through a relative path, such as `workspace:../lib`, has `catalog:` dependencies. Their catalog entries now resolve the way they do for a package injected by name [#​17280](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17280).

- `pnpm dedupe` now refreshes cached registry metadata while re-resolving locked versions [#​17208](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17208).

- `pnpm dedupe --check` no longer fails when the only difference is a `deprecated` notice that the registry added or removed after the lockfile was written [#​17198](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17198).

- Installs delegated to a pnpr server now resolve every prefix declared for a registry URL. A dependency or lockfile entry that used the second of two prefixes for the same registry, such as `zeta:` next to `work:` in `namedRegistries`, failed on the server [pnpm/tasks#204](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/204).

- Registry revisions are now addressed at `<registry>/<name>@<version>+r<revision>` [pnpm/tasks#208](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/208).

##### Adding packages and global packages

- `pnpm add <pkg>@<tag>` and `pnpm add <pkg>@<range>` now install the version the tag or range resolves to, even when the saved range allows a newer one [#​17234](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17234).

- `pnpm add <pkg>` without a version now installs the version under the dist-tag set by the `tag` setting. An `npm:` alias or a `jsr:` dependency without a version resolves that tag too. The setting is read from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, the global config, `PNPM_CONFIG_TAG`, and `--config.tag`, and defaults to `latest`.

- `pnpm add` now accepts the lowercase short options `-p`, `-d`, `-o`, and `-e` as aliases of `--save-prod`, `--save-dev`, `--save-optional`, and `--save-exact`.

- `pnpm -D install <pkg>` now saves the package to devDependencies. An `add` option such as `-D` or `-E` written before `install <pkg>` was rejected as an unexpected argument.

- `pnpm add -T` now reports that the short option is ambiguous and points to `--save-types` and `--tilde`.

- Global packages installed with `pnpm add -g` are now linked from the global virtual store, so global packages that share dependencies share one copy. Set `virtualStoreType: project` to give each global install its own virtual store.

- `pnpm add -g` and the other `--global` commands now fail with `ERR_PNPM_CONFIG_CONFLICT_VIRTUAL_STORE_DIR_WITH_GLOBAL` when `--virtual-store-dir` is passed. A custom `--hoist-pattern` fails with `ERR_PNPM_CONFIG_CONFLICT_HOIST_PATTERN_WITH_GLOBAL`. Passing `--link-workspace-packages`, `--shared-workspace-lockfile`, or `--config.lockfile-dir` with `--global` also fails, with the matching `ERR_PNPM_CONFIG_CONFLICT_*_WITH_GLOBAL` code.

##### Registries, proxies, and login

- pnpm now reads the `strictSsl` and `localAddress` settings from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, the global `config.yaml`, `PNPM_CONFIG_*` environment variables, and `--config.*` options. This includes `pnpm self-update` and the download of the pnpm version pinned in `packageManager`. Before, pnpm read them only from `.npmrc` as `strict-ssl` and `local-address` and ignored the other sources [pnpm/tasks#201](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/201).

- When Corepack runs pnpm and the native binary has to be downloaded, the download now uses the proxy from pnpm's config. That proxy comes from `PNPM_CONFIG_HTTPS_PROXY` and the matching variables, the global `config.yaml`, and the user `.npmrc`. Previously, the download read the proxy only from `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, and `NO_PROXY` [pnpm/tasks#215](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/215).

- When the `pnpm` package downloads its native binary on first run, as it does under Corepack, it now trusts the CA certificates from the `ca`, `ca[]`, and `cafile` settings of `.npmrc`, including the ones scoped to the registry. A registry behind a private CA failed with `fetch failed` before, unless `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` named the CA. A project `.npmrc` is used only while the download is checked against npm's signature. Node.js versions that cannot add CA certificates after startup still need `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`.

- `pnpm login` saves the token in `<pnpm config>/auth.ini` again. Since v12.1.0, an unscoped login had made its registry the default for every project that did not name a registry. A login now also removes the token an earlier login saved for that registry or scope under `_auth` in the global `config.yaml`. `pnpm login --scope` still routes the scope through the global `registries` setting.

- pnpm no longer warns that a `registries` entry routed through the `@` scope matches no configured registry. pnpm applied such an entry and its options such as `serverType` while reporting it as ignored [pnpm/tasks#184](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/184).

##### Running scripts and other commands

- `pnpm ci --lockfile` and `pnpm ci --config.lockfile=true` no longer delete `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `pnpm ci` now always keeps the lockfile and runs a frozen install from it.

- `pnpm deploy --legacy` now checks the workspace lockfile against `minimumReleaseAge` and the other resolution policies, as `pnpm install` does, and fails with `ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION` when a locked version is too new. It used to deploy an older version that is not in the lockfile without a warning [#​17209](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17209).

- `pnpm deploy` now keeps a deployed symlink to a directory inside the project even if the directory is not among the deployed files, such as a link into `node_modules` [#​17288](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17288).

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now keep `pnpm.config` in the published `package.json`. They also always include the file `pnpm.config` points to in the tarball [#​17210](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17210).

- `pnpm -r publish --batch` now sends `PUT /-/pnpr/v0/publish`, the batch publish endpoint that pnpr serves.

- `pnpm audit --ignore` and `pnpm audit --ignore-unfixable` now exit with a non-zero code when vulnerabilities at or above the audit level remain after ignoring. Before, these commands always exited with code 0.

- `pnpm audit --fix` and `pnpm audit --interactive` now fail with `ERR_PNPM_AUDIT_FIX_WITH_IGNORE` when combined with `--ignore` or `--ignore-unfixable`. Before, the fix ran and the ignore flags had no effect.

- `pnpm -r run <script>` now honors the `requiredScripts` setting from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. If the script is listed there and a selected project does not define it, the run fails with `ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_NO_SCRIPT` and names the projects that lack it.

- `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` no longer report the dependencies as out of date after a lockfile change when `dedupePeers` is `true` [#​17322](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17322).

- On macOS, killing pnpm while it runs scripts in several projects at once now ends every one of those scripts. Before, a script could keep running after pnpm died.

- `pnpm run`, `pnpm exec`, and `pnpm dlx` no longer dump a core file for `pnpm` itself when a command they started dies from a signal [#​17204](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17204).

- The `runtime` setting is now read. Setting `runtime: false` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `pnpm_config_runtime=false`, or `--config.runtime=false` stops `pnpm install`, `pnpm add`, `pnpm dedupe`, and the other installing commands from installing the runtimes in `devEngines.runtime` and `engines.runtime`. `pnpm dedupe` now also accepts `--no-runtime`.

- Directory selectors with `legacyDirFiltering: true` now include the project in the named directory along with its descendants. Excluding a directory also excludes that project [pnpm/tasks#196](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/196).

- `pnpm help --all` and `pnpm help -a` now print the full list of commands. They used to fail with an "unrecognized subcommand" error.

- Reading the file-creation mask on Linux no longer sets it. pnpm had to replace the mask to learn what it was, and a file another thread created in the window between the two calls was created unmasked.

- pnpm now passes an interrupt on to the handler it replaced, with the arguments that handler expects. A handler that asked for the signal's details was called without them. Only a program that embeds pnpm and installs its own `SIGINT`, `SIGTERM` or `SIGHUP` handler was affected.

##### Store

- `pnpm store prune` now keeps the packages that a project still uses when pnpm copied or cloned them into `node_modules`. These include patched packages, built packages, and every package installed with `packageImportMethod: copy`. Before, the prune removed them, and the next install downloaded them again [#​7192](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/7192).

- `pnpm store prune` now keeps the packages of a project when the store path reaches its directory through a symlink. Previously, prune dropped such a project from its list and removed the packages only that project used from the global virtual store.

- `pnpm store prune` now removes the package metadata cache, the `metadata*` directories in the cache directory. This clears the outdated integrity checksums that cause `ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_INTEGRITY` when a registry republishes a version.

- `pnpm install` resolves dependencies faster in large workspaces on Linux, macOS, and Windows on x64 and arm64.

### Configuration and setting up pnpm

- Registry credentials and TLS settings passed with `--config`, such as `--config.//registry.example.com/:_authToken=<token>`, are now applied. They take precedence over the same settings in `.npmrc` files.

- pnpm now reads only the settings it needs to decide whether to switch to the pnpm version a project pins. A setting outside them can no longer fail that decision or change its outcome. For example, `pnpm --version` no longer fails in a pinned project whose `pnpm-workspace.yaml` has a setting this pnpm cannot read. Projects that pin neither pnpm nor a runtime skip this check without reading any settings.

- When pnpm switches to the version a project pins, an option only the pinned pnpm knows now reaches that pnpm when it comes immediately before the command name, as in `pnpm --new-flag install`. When switching for `pnpm --version` or an unrecognized command line, pnpm also honors `--color`, `--no-color`, `--reporter`, and `--loglevel` wherever they appear on the command line.

- `pnpm self-update` now updates the project's pnpm pin when Homebrew installed pnpm or Corepack runs it, leaving the global pnpm alone [#​17001](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17001). Run inside a workspace package, `pnpm self-update` updates the pin in the workspace root's manifest, including in `package.yaml` or `package.json5`.

- `pnpm setup` now completes when Windows registry environment values cannot be read or written. It prints PowerShell commands to configure `PNPM_HOME` and `PATH` without registry access [#​17167](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17167).

- `pnpm setup` now succeeds when it cannot tell which shell configuration file to update, for example in a container where `SHELL` is not set. It installs pnpm and prints the `PNPM_HOME` and `PATH` lines to add yourself. Previously it failed with `ERR_PNPM_UNKNOWN_SHELL`, and so did the installer script at get.pnpm.io [#​16973](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16973).

- In StackBlitz WebContainers, `pnpm` no longer crashes intermittently with `Parking not supported on this platform`, and running a command that does not exist now reports that the command was not found. Previously it sometimes failed with a generic error.

### [`v1.106.1`](https://redirect.github.com/sass/dart-sass/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#11061)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/sass/dart-sass/compare/1.106.0...1.106.1)

- Fix a bug where an attribute selector with an empty value (such as
  `[class=""]`) would crash when serializing.

- Don't crash when serializing a number with an empty unit. This is only
  possible through the JavaScript and Dart APIs or the embedded protocol.

##### Embedded Dart Sass

- More robustly convert invalid value errors into `PARAMS` errors.

### [`v1.106.0`](https://redirect.github.com/sass/dart-sass/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#11060)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/sass/dart-sass/compare/1.105.2...1.106.0)

- Don't normalize CSS escapes in statement contexts that can contain
  interpolation. For example, `@f\6Fo` is now emitted as written rather than
  normalized to `@foo`.

- Fix a bug where quotes would be removed from attribute selector values that
  contained backslashes.

- Fix invalid source spans that could cause crashes when encountering a syntax
  error in selectors or media queries that also contain escape sequences.

- Fix a bug where the indented syntax parser would crash when parsing a file
  where the first statement was indented *and* appeared after the first line.

- Fix a bug that could cause crashes when encountering errors or warnings in
  interpolations that contain patterns like `// */`.

- **Potentially breaking compatibility fix:** CSS escape codes whose values are
  0, for Unicode surrogates, or greater than the maximum allowed code point are
  now consistently normalized to U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER in expression
  contexts. Previously, in some cases these were instead normalized to the
  normalized form of the original escape sequence, which violates the principle
  that all escape sequences for identical values should be normalized the same
  way. In other cases, these would simply throw errors.

  As a special case, `\0` on its own will continue to be normalized to `\0 ` to
  support historical CSS hacks.

- **Potentially breaking bug fix:** Throw an error for mixins and functions that
  have rest parameters which are the same as normal parameters. Previously, the
  positional parameters wouldn't be accessible and calling such a mixin or
  function with a named argument would crash the compiler.

- **Potentially breaking bug fix:** Fix various cases where using a CSS escape
  code at the beginning of an identifier would change parsing behavior versus
  using the character directly.

- **Potentially breaking bug fix:** When a number's unit is ambiguous with a
  numeric exponent, the unit is now serialized as an escape code rather than a
  literal `e` to avoid being interpreted as an exponent by CSS.

- **Potentially breaking bug fix:** Don't parse a CSS escape code for U+45 LATIN
  CAPITAL LETTER E or U+65 LATIN LOWERCASE LETTER E as an exponent in
  `@keyframes` percentage selectors.

- **Potentially breaking bug fix:** Properly normalize underscores written as
  CSS escape codes in variable, mixin, and function names.

Issues.Title: fix(material/chips): avoid clipping icon avatars
Issues.Body: Icons used with matChipAvatar were clipped by the avatar's circular shape because mat-icon hides its overflow; the icon is now allowed to overflow so its corners render, while image avatars and app-styled backgrounds keep the avatar shape. The chips docs now state that the leading slot accepts icons, and icon spacing is left unchanged to avoid layout shifts. **Screenshots of before and after this change:** **Notes**: - The fix sets `overflow: visible` on `mat-icon` avatars instead of removing their `border-radius`. Removing the radius would turn app-styled circular icon backgrounds into squares (third screenshot). - `mat-icon` normally hides its overflow (#11826). Inside a chip, the leading slot already hides its own overflow and ignores pointer events, so that protection is kept. - Image avatars, text avatars, the selection checkmark, edit and remove buttons, and chip dimensions are unchanged. I checked this with computed styles and pixel diffs in M2 and M3, LTR and RTL, and dense layouts. - Icon spacing (the issue's 8px/8px point) is intentionally unchanged. Changing it would alter the width of every chip with an icon, and the same slot also holds the selection checkmark. Happy to handle it in a follow-up, if desired. Fixes #31628.
